text:
Aisha (People Ops): Quick one  Rajeev just had his baby in India (2026-08-15) and is flying back this week. Wants to add newborn to benefits. No SSN yet, birth cert in Gujarati with local stamp. What docs do we accept and can coverage be backdated to birth?
Rajeev S: Hi team  baby born 8/15, passport applied, birth cert only in Gujarati, hospital discharge docs in English, coming back 8/22. How soon can I enroll?
Marta - Benefits: Congrats! Birth is a qualifying life event. You have 30 days from the birth to submit QLE docs to enroll outside open enrollment. Carriers usually allow effective date as of date of birth (8/15) if docs support it.
Rajeev S: We only have foreign birth cert (Gujarati) and hospital discharge with English summary. The birth cert has an official stamp but no apostille yet. Is that okay?
Marta - Benefits: For foreign documents we typically require either: (1) a consular report of birth abroad (CRBA) or passport showing birth, or (2) foreign birth certificate plus certified English translation and apostille or legalization, depending on the country. Some carriers accept hospital record + passport application receipt temporarily. We'll escalate to carrier if needed.
ComplianceBot: Note  if translation is provided, it must be certified (translator affidavit) and include translator contact info. Do not post PHI publicly. Use the secure HR upload.
TranslatorService: We can certify an English translation within 24-48 hours. Fee applies. Send scanned birth cert via secure link and we'll return certified PDF.
Aisha (People Ops): Rajeev, please upload the birth cert, hospital discharge, and passport application receipt to https://hr.redwood.com/upload (select "QLE - Newborn - Foreign docs"). Redact any full SSNs.
Rajeev S: Uploading now. If SSN arrives late, will that block enrollment?
Marta - Benefits: Carriers require a tax identifier for final enrollment/ID cards. We can provisionally enroll the child pending SSN for up to 60 days in many cases, but policies vary by carrier. If SSN isn't provided within the carrier window we may have to cancel retro coverage. We'll note the provisional status and request SSN as soon as you have it.
Noah (Payroll): Payroll note: if coverage is approved effective 8/15, we'll calculate retro premiums and can spread the adjustment over upcoming paychecks at employee's choice. If SSN delays finalization, premium reconciliation still proceeds once enrollment is confirmed.
Rajeev S: Thanks. If apostille isn't possible quickly, will CRBA with passport be sufficient?
Marta - Benefits: Yes, CRBA or infant passport showing nationality/birth details is typically the easiest for US-born-abroad or foreign-born dependents. If you don't have those, certified translation + apostille is the alternative. We'll work with carrier for flexibility given timing.
ComplianceBot: Reminder  use secure upload only. We'll store docs encrypted and limit access to Benefits/People Ops. Redact IDs where not needed.
